title: components: `element:record_picker` renders a label element with no `htmlFor` against a trigger with no `id` — the caption its own docs advertise names nothing
body:
Found while implementing #5735 (the sibling gap on `element:text_input`, PR #5770). Out of that card's fence — filed, not fixed there. Unassigned.

## Dedup performed before filing

Semantic search over this repo returned the family but nothing covering this block: #3341 (closed — `InlineCreateRelated` plus the `custom` ActionParamDialog select branch), #3976 and #3306 (closed — the form renderer's builtin `select`), #3991 (**open** — the form renderer's empty-options / dependency-gate branch putting the host id on a div). All of those are the *form* renderer or the *custom* dialog. None is `element:record_picker`.

Note for whoever searches next: `search_issues` in this fleet is **semantic**, and it takes `owner` / `repo` as parameters. Passing GitHub search qualifiers (`repo:...`, `is:open`) inside the query string returns **zero for everything**, including terms known to be present in an open issue — a silent false-clean. The REST `/search/issues` endpoint is blocked for these sessions entirely ("sessions are bound to their configured repositories"), so it cannot be used as the second instrument.

## Measured

`packages/components/src/renderers/basic/record-picker.tsx`, render body:

```tsx
{label && <label className="text-sm font-medium text-foreground">{label}</label>}
<Select value={value} onValueChange={handleChange} disabled={loading || !!error || !object}>
  <SelectTrigger className="w-full max-w-xs" data-testid="record-picker-trigger">
```

The label element carries **no `htmlFor`**, and the `SelectTrigger` carries **no `id`**. A repo-scoped grep for `htmlFor` and `aria-` across that whole file returns zero hits of either (controlled — the same grep pattern returns the `Label` / `htmlFor` pair from `text-input.tsx` next door, so the zero is a reading).

So the association is missing from **both** ends. This is a step worse than the `element:text_input` gap #5735 closes: there the `label` half was correctly wired and only `description` was adrift. Here the caption names nothing at all, and the picker has no accessible name unless a `placeholder` happens to supply one.

The block's own registration prose advertises the wiring the code does not do — `record-picker.tsx:358`:

> 'Caption rendered above the picker, in a `label` element. Display-only …'

A `label` element with no association is not a caption for the control; it is styled text that happens to use a `label` tag.

## Why this reads as a defect and not a nice-to-have

The platform has already ruled on this exact class and fixed three instances of it: #3341 gave the ActionParamDialog's `SelectTrigger` the `id` its `Label` already pointed at, and #3976 / #3306 dealt with the form renderer's builtin `select`. The reasoning in #3341's landed test file transfers verbatim — `SelectTrigger` renders a `button` with `role="combobox"`, and `button` is a labelable element, so a plain `htmlFor` / `id` pair is the correct association with no `aria-labelledby` needed (Radix sets none on the trigger).

`element:record_picker` is also the block `element:text_input`'s own module header names as its complement ("the data-entry complement to element:record_picker"), so the two sit side by side in a pure-SDUI page with opposite a11y behaviour.

## What a fix would decide (for triage, not decided here)

1. **Where the trigger's id comes from.** The picker's `schema?.id` is optional, exactly as on `element:text_input` — it is already read for `usePageVariableBinding(schema?.id)` and published as `data-picker-id`. #5735 resolved the analogous question by observing that `htmlFor` needs an id on the *control* (author-supplied, so the wiring can only hold when the author gave one) while `aria-describedby` needs one on an element the renderer owns. Here it is squarely the first case, so "wire only when `schema.id` exists" matches both the `element:text_input` precedent and #3341's shape — but minting a `useId` fallback so the picker is *always* named is a defensible alternative, and the two answers differ.
2. **Whether the `label` element is right at all.** #3341 concluded `htmlFor` / `id` is correct against a `SelectTrigger`, so this is likely just the missing pair rather than a switch to `aria-labelledby` — worth confirming against Radix's current trigger output rather than assuming.

A fix should pin the resolution (the label resolves to the combobox, and the combobox's accessible name is the label), not the two attributes separately — the failure mode #3341's test file documents is an association that looks wired and resolves to nothing.

## Refs

- #5735 / PR #5770 — the sibling gap on `element:text_input`, where this was found
- #3341 — the same class, ruled and fixed on two other surfaces
- #3976, #3306, #3991 — the form renderer's instances of the class
